at bade.explanation: "At bade" means "to bathe" and also "to swim", going into the sea or a lake for fun or to cool off. It is not for racing or training laps.

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **bade** i havet i dag.
sentence.en: We would like to swim in the sea today.

at bage.explanation: "At bage" means "to bake", for things like cakes and bread. Do not mix it up with at stege (to fry), which is what you do with meat or eggs in a pan.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **bage** en kage i ovnen.
sentence.en: I want to bake a cake in the oven.

at bande.explanation: "At bande" means "to swear (curse)", saying rude words when you are angry. To swear a promise, use at sværge (to swear): Jeg sværger (I swear).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **bande** foran børnene.
sentence.en: You must not swear in front of the children.

at banke på.explanation: "At banke på" means "to knock", for example on a door. Without på, at banke means to beat: Hjertet banker (The heart beats).

sentence.da: Du skal **banke på**, når døren er lukket.
sentence.en: You have to knock when the door is closed.

at barbere sig.explanation: "At barbere sig" means "to shave", taking the hair off your face or body with a razor. Sig shows that you do it to yourself. To shave someone else, leave it out: Jeg barberer ham (I shave him).

sentence.da: Han har skæg og vil **barbere sig**.
sentence.en: He has a beard and wants to shave.

at bede.explanation: "At bede" means "to ask" when you want something done or given. It also means "to pray": Hun beder til Gud (She prays to God). To ask a question, use at spørge (to ask a question).

sentence.da: Må jeg **bede** dig om hjælp?
sentence.en: May I ask you for help?

at bede om.explanation: "At bede om" means "to ask for" something you would like to get. Om comes before the thing you want. To ask a question, use at spørge (to ask).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **bede om** en kop kaffe.
sentence.en: I would like to ask for a cup of coffee.

at begynde.explanation: "At begynde" means "to begin" or "to start". You can use it with another action: Jeg begynder at læse (I begin to read). It also works alone: Skolen begynder i august (School begins in August).

sentence.da: Filmen skal **begynde** klokken otte.
sentence.en: The film is going to start at eight.

at begynde på.explanation: "At begynde på" means "to begin on" something new, like a task, a job or a course. It is close to at starte på (to start on).

sentence.da: Efter ferien skal jeg **begynde på** universitetet.
sentence.en: After the vacation, I am going to start at the university.

at behandle.explanation: "At behandle" means "to treat", both in medicine and in how you act toward people: Han behandler mig godt (He treats me well). It also means to handle a matter officially: Kommunen behandler sagen (The city is handling the case).

sentence.da: Lægen kan **behandle** sygdommen med medicin.
sentence.en: The doctor can treat the illness with medicine.

at beholde.explanation: "At beholde" means "to keep" something you already have. For a promise, use at holde (to hold): Jeg holder mit løfte (I keep my promise).

sentence.da: Du må gerne **beholde** bogen.
sentence.en: You may keep the book.

at behøve.explanation: "At behøve" means "to need", and it is mostly used for needing to do something, usually with at (to): Du behøver ikke at komme (You do not need to come). For needing a thing, Danes usually say at have brug for: Jeg har brug for hjælp (I need help).

sentence.da: Du vil ikke **behøve** at betale.
sentence.en: You will not need to pay.

at bekræfte.explanation: "At bekræfte" means "to confirm", saying that something is true or settled. It also works for showing that a guess was right: Testen bekræfter det (The test confirms it).

sentence.da: Kan du **bekræfte**, at mødet er klokken ti?
sentence.en: Can you confirm that the meeting is at ten o'clock?

at bekymre sig.explanation: "At bekymre sig" means "to worry", feeling uneasy about something that might go wrong. Add om for what you worry about: Jeg bekymrer mig om dig (I worry about you). Sig shows that the worry is yours.

sentence.da: Hun vil ikke **bekymre sig**, fordi alt går godt.
sentence.en: She won't worry because everything is going well.

at beskrive.explanation: "At beskrive" means "to describe". It is built from at skrive (to write), but it does not need paper: Kan du beskrive vejen til stationen? (Can you describe the way to the station?)

sentence.da: Kan du **beskrive** manden for politiet?
sentence.en: Can you describe the man for the police?

at beskytte.explanation: "At beskytte" means "to protect". Add mod (against) to say from what: Vi beskytter huset mod regn (We protect the house against rain).

sentence.da: Du skal **beskytte** huden mod solen.
sentence.en: You need to protect your skin from the sun.

at beslutte.explanation: "At beslutte" means "to decide", and it is often followed by at and an action: Vi besluttede at blive hjemme (We decided to stay home). To say you made up your mind, add mig: Jeg har besluttet mig (I have made up my mind).

sentence.da: Vi skal **beslutte**, hvor vi vil spise i aften.
sentence.en: We have to decide where we want to eat tonight.

at beslutte sig.explanation: "At beslutte sig" means "to decide", or to make up your mind. To say what you chose, add for: Jeg besluttede mig for at blive (I decided to stay).

sentence.da: Hun skal **beslutte sig** inden i morgen.
sentence.en: She has to decide before tomorrow.

at bestemme.explanation: "At bestemme" means "to decide". It also means to be the one in charge: Hvem bestemmer her? (Who decides here?)

sentence.da: Du må **bestemme**, hvad vi skal spise.
sentence.en: You get to decide what we eat.

at bestemme sig.explanation: "At bestemme sig" means "to make up one's mind". Without sig, at bestemme means "to decide for others": Chefen bestemmer (The boss decides).

forms.en: I have made up my mind

sentence.da: Han skal **bestemme sig** i dag.
sentence.en: He has to make up his mind today.

at bestille.explanation: "At bestille" means "to order" or "to book", for example food or a table: Jeg vil gerne bestille et bord (I would like to book a table). To ask for a meal, you can also say Jeg vil gerne have... (I would like to have...).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **bestille** en pizza.
sentence.en: I would like to order a pizza.

at bestille tid.explanation: "At bestille tid" means "to make an appointment", for example at the doctor, dentist or hairdresser. Literally, it is to order time: bestille (to book) and tid (time). To say who with, add hos (at / with): bestille tid hos lægen (make an appointment with the doctor).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **bestille tid** hos lægen.
sentence.en: I would like to make an appointment with the doctor.

at bestå.explanation: "At bestå" means "to pass" a test: Hun bestod prøven (She passed the test). With af, it means "to consist of": Holdet består af ti spillere (The team consists of ten players).

sentence.da: Hun skal læse meget for at **bestå** eksamen.
sentence.en: She has to study a lot to pass the exam.

at besøge.explanation: "At besøge" means "to visit". You put the person or place straight after it, with no word for "to": Jeg besøger Anna (I visit Anna). You can also say komme på besøg (to come for a visit).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **besøge** min mormor i dag.
sentence.en: I want to visit my grandmother today.

at betale.explanation: "At betale" means "to pay". Say what you pay for with for: Jeg betaler for billetten (I pay for the ticket). The amount comes straight after it: Jeg betaler hundrede kroner (I pay a hundred kroner).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **betale** 40 kroner for kaffen.
sentence.en: I have to pay 40 kroner for the coffee.

at betale for.explanation: "At betale for" means "to pay for". For points to what the money buys: Jeg betaler for maden (I am paying for the food). With a person after it, you cover their share: Jeg betaler for dig (I am paying for you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **betale for** kaffen.
sentence.en: I would like to pay for the coffee.

at betale med kort.explanation: "At betale med kort" means "to pay by card". Med means "with", so it is literally to pay with card. To pay in cash, say at betale kontant (to pay in cash).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **betale med kort**.
sentence.en: I would like to pay by card.

at betale tilbage.explanation: "At betale tilbage" means "to pay back": Jeg betaler pengene tilbage (I pay the money back). To say who gets it, put the person after betale: Jeg betaler dig tilbage (I pay you back).

sentence.da: Jeg har lånt penge og skal **betale tilbage**.
sentence.en: I borrowed money and have to pay back.

at betyde.explanation: "At betyde" means "to mean": Hvad betyder det? (What does that mean?). You answer with Det betyder... (It means...). It can also mean "to matter": Det betyder meget for mig (It means a lot to me).

sentence.da: Hvad kan det ord **betyde**?
sentence.en: What can that word mean?

at bevæge.explanation: "At bevæge" means "to move" something, like a body part. To move yourself, add sig: Han bevæger sig langsomt (He moves slowly). To move house, use at flytte (to move).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **bevæge** min venstre arm.
sentence.en: I cannot move my left arm.

at bevæge sig.explanation: "At bevæge sig" means "to move" your own body. To move a thing or move house, use at flytte (to move): Jeg flytter bordet (I am moving the table).

sentence.da: Katten kan ikke **bevæge sig**, fordi den sidder fast.
sentence.en: The cat cannot move because it is stuck.

at bide.explanation: "At bide" means "to bite", cutting into something with your teeth. It works for people, animals and insects: Myggen bed mig (The mosquito bit me).

sentence.da: Hunden kan **bide** med sine skarpe tænder.
sentence.en: The dog can bite with its sharp teeth.

at binde.explanation: "At binde" means "to tie" or "to bind": you fasten something with a lace, string or rope so it stays in place. Jeg binder håret op (I tie my hair up).

sentence.da: Vi skal **binde** hunden til træet.
sentence.en: We have to tie the dog to the tree.

at binde snørebånd.explanation: "At binde snørebånd" means "to tie shoelaces". It is built from at binde (to tie) and snørebånd (shoelaces), and the same verb works for other things: at binde et tørklæde (to tie a scarf).

sentence.da: Min lille datter kan allerede **binde snørebånd**.
sentence.en: My little daughter can already tie shoelaces.

at blaffe.explanation: "At blaffe" means "to hitchhike", to travel by asking drivers to take you along for free.

sentence.da: Vi har ingen bil, men vi vil **blaffe** til kysten.
sentence.en: We have no car, but we want to hitchhike to the coast.

at blande.explanation: "At blande" means "to mix". With sig added, it means to interfere: Bland dig ikke i det (Do not interfere in it).

sentence.da: Du skal **blande** mel og æg i en skål.
sentence.en: You have to mix flour and eggs in a bowl.

at blande sig.explanation: "At blande sig" means "to interfere", taking part where you are not wanted. Plain at blande means "to mix": Jeg blander mel og vand (I mix flour and water).

sentence.da: Han skal ikke **blande sig** i det.
sentence.en: He should not interfere in that.

at blive.explanation: "At blive" means "to become" and also "to stay": Han bliver læge (He becomes a doctor) and Jeg bliver hjemme (I stay at home). It is also used for what will happen: Det bliver godt (It will be good). At være (to be) only says what is true right now.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **blive** læge.
sentence.en: I want to become a doctor.

at blive bange.explanation: "At blive bange" means "to get scared". Blive (to become) shows the change from calm to scared. To say you are scared right now, use at være bange (to be scared). Add what scares you with for: bange for hunde (afraid of dogs).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **blive bange**, når det tordner.
sentence.en: I can get scared when it thunders.

at blive enige.explanation: "At blive enige" means "to agree", when two or more people come to the same decision, so it needs more than one person. To give your own opinion, say Jeg er enig (I agree).

sentence.da: Vi skal **blive enige** om en pris.
sentence.en: We have to agree on a price.

at blive forelsket.explanation: "At blive forelsket" means "to fall in love", and you add i for the person: Hun blev forelsket i sin kollega (She fell in love with her coworker). Being in love already is at være forelsket.

sentence.da: Jeg er ved at **blive forelsket** i hende.
sentence.en: I am falling in love with her.

at blive færdig.explanation: "At blive færdig" means "to finish", as in be done: Jeg bliver færdig klokken fem (I will be done at five). With a job title it means to graduate: Hun bliver færdig som læge (She is graduating as a doctor).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **blive færdig** før frokost.
sentence.en: I would like to be done before lunch.

at blive gammel.explanation: "At blive gammel" means "to grow old". Blive means "to become", so it fits other changes too: at blive kold (to get cold), at blive stor (to grow big).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **blive gammel** og rask.
sentence.en: I would like to grow old and stay healthy.

at blive gift.explanation: "At blive gift" means "to get married", the moment of marrying. To say you are already married, use at være gift (to be married). Add the person with med (with): at blive gift med ham (to marry him).

sentence.da: Vi skal **blive gift** i sommer.
sentence.en: We are going to get married this summer.

at blive glad.explanation: "At blive glad" means "to become happy", the moment you feel pleased. Add for (about) to say what pleased you: Jeg blev glad for kagen (I was happy about the cake). Jeg er glad (I am happy) is about how you feel now.

sentence.da: Hun vil **blive glad**, når hun ser gaven.
sentence.en: She will be happy when she sees the gift.

at blive hjemme.explanation: "At blive hjemme" means "to stay home". Blive means "to stay" here, and "hjemme" means "at home".

sentence.da: Syge børn skal **blive hjemme**.
sentence.en: Sick children have to stay home.

at blive overrasket.explanation: "At blive overrasket" means "to be surprised". Add over (by) to say what surprised you: Hun blev overrasket over nyheden (She was surprised by the news).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **blive overrasket** på min fødselsdag.
sentence.en: I would like to be surprised on my birthday.

at blive rask.explanation: "At blive rask" means "to get better" after being sick. Rask means "healthy" or "recovered". To someone who is ill you can say God bedring! (Get well soon!).

sentence.da: Du vil snart **blive rask**.
sentence.en: You will soon get better.

at blive skilt.explanation: "At blive skilt" means "to get divorced" and describes the event. To say what someone is now, use fraskilt: Han er fraskilt (He is divorced).

sentence.da: Mine forældre skal **blive skilt** næste år.
sentence.en: My parents are going to get divorced next year.

at blive syg.explanation: "At blive syg" means "to get sick", the moment you fall ill. At være syg (to be sick) describes the state you are in afterwards.

sentence.da: Uden søvn kan man **blive syg**.
sentence.en: Without sleep you can get sick.

at blive til.explanation: "At blive til" means "to become" or "to turn into": Larven blev til en sommerfugl (The caterpillar turned into a butterfly). Til (into) names what it becomes, while plain blive goes with a description: Han blev træt (He got tired).

sentence.da: Vand kan **blive til** is.
sentence.en: Water can turn into ice.

at blive træt.explanation: "At blive træt" means "to get tired", the change from not tired to tired. To say you are tired right now, use at være træt (to be tired).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **blive træt** af at løbe.
sentence.en: I can get tired from running.

at blive venner.explanation: "At blive venner" means "to become friends". It always uses venner (friends), never ven, because two or more people are involved: Maria og jeg blev venner (Maria and I became friends).

sentence.da: Jeg tror, vi kan **blive venner**.
sentence.en: I think we can become friends.

at blive vred.explanation: "At blive vred" means "to get angry", the moment it happens. Being angry for a while is at være vred: Han er vred (He is angry).

sentence.da: Han kan **blive vred**, hvis jeg kommer for sent.
sentence.en: He can get angry if I am late.

at blive væk.explanation: "At blive væk" means "to stay away" and "to go missing": Han blev væk fra mødet (He stayed away from the meeting). Min nøgle er blevet væk (My key has gone missing).

forms.en: I have stayed away / gone missing

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **blive væk** fra festen.
sentence.en: I do not want to stay away from the party.

at blomstre.explanation: "At blomstre" means "to bloom", for flowers and trees that open. It can also mean doing well: Byen blomstrer (The town is thriving).

sentence.da: Roserne vil **blomstre** i juni.
sentence.en: The roses will bloom in June.

at blæse.explanation: "At blæse" means "to blow", for wind and for blowing with your mouth: Jeg blæser lysene ud (I blow the candles out).

sentence.da: Det kan **blæse** meget på stranden.
sentence.en: It can blow a lot on the beach.

at bløde.explanation: "At bløde" means "to bleed". To say which part bleeds, add fra (from): Hun blødte fra næsen (Her nose was bleeding).

sentence.da: Han faldt og begyndte at **bløde**.
sentence.en: He fell and began to bleed.

at bo.explanation: "At bo" means "to live" in the sense of where your home is. For being alive, use at leve (to live, be alive): Min farmor lever stadig (My grandmother is still alive).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **bo** tæt på skolen.
sentence.en: I want to live close to the school.

at bo sammen.explanation: "At bo sammen" means "to live together". Without sammen (together), Jeg bor i Aarhus (I live in Aarhus) just says where you live.

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **bo sammen** i en lille lejlighed.
sentence.en: We would like to live together in a small apartment.

at bokse.explanation: "At bokse" means "to box", as a sport. A person who does it is en bokser (a boxer).

sentence.da: Min bror vil gerne **bokse** i en klub.
sentence.en: My brother would like to box at a club.

at booke.explanation: "At booke" means "to book", for a room, a table or a trip. It is close to at reservere (to reserve).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **booke** et bord til fredag.
sentence.en: I want to book a table for Friday.

at bore.explanation: "At bore" means "to drill", to make a hole in a wall or in wood. The power tool is en boremaskine (a drill).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **bore** et hul i væggen.
sentence.en: I have to drill a hole in the wall.

at bremse.explanation: "At bremse" means "to slow down", and also "to brake" in a car or on a bike. It works for anything you slow down: Regnen bremser os (The rain slows us down).

sentence.da: Du skal **bremse**, når lyset er rødt.
sentence.en: You have to brake when the light is red.

at bringe.explanation: "At bringe" means "to bring", but it sounds a bit formal. In daily talk, Danes say Jeg tager kaffe med (I'm bringing coffee). Bringe still shows up in bringe i fare (to put in danger).

sentence.da: Han vil **bringe** gaven til dig i morgen.
sentence.en: He will bring the gift to you tomorrow.

at brokke sig.explanation: "At brokke sig" means "to complain" or "to grumble" about small everyday things: Han brokker sig over vejret (He grumbles about the weather). The little word over (about) names what bothers you.

sentence.da: Min bror plejer at **brokke sig** over maden.
sentence.en: My brother usually grumbles about the food.

at bruge.explanation: "At bruge" means "to use", for example a tool or a phone. It also means "to spend" money or time: Jeg bruger mange penge (I spend a lot of money). What comes after it tells you which meaning is meant.

sentence.da: Du kan **bruge** en kniv til brød.
sentence.en: You can use a knife for bread.

at bruge op.explanation: "At bruge op" means "to use up", so nothing is left. Op adds that idea of finishing, as in at spise op (to eat up) and at drikke op (to drink up). Plain at bruge (to use) only says you used something.

sentence.da: Vi må **bruge op**, hvad vi har i køleskabet.
sentence.en: We have to use up what we have in the fridge.

at bruge penge.explanation: "At bruge penge" means "to spend money". At bruge (to use) also means "to spend", so at bruge penge på noget is to spend money on something. Penge (money) is used without en or et (a).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **bruge penge** på en jakke.
sentence.en: I would like to spend money on a jacket.

at bryde.explanation: "At bryde" means "to break", mostly for promises, rules and silence: Han brød sit løfte (He broke his promise). Watch out: brød also means bread, as in et brød (a loaf).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **bryde** reglerne i spillet.
sentence.en: You must not break the rules of the game.

at bryde et løfte.explanation: "At bryde et løfte" means "to break a promise", so you do not do what you said you would. Bryde is also used for rules: at bryde en regel (to break a rule).

sentence.da: Han vil aldrig **bryde et løfte**.
sentence.en: He will never break a promise.

at brække.explanation: "At brække" means "to break (a bone)": Hun brækkede armen (She broke her arm). To vomit, add sig: at brække sig (to throw up): Han brækkede sig (He threw up). For a glass or plate, say at gå i stykker (to break): Glasset gik i stykker (The glass broke).

sentence.da: Pas på, du kan **brække** benet på isen.
sentence.en: Be careful, you can break your leg on the ice.

at brænde.explanation: "At brænde" means "to burn", for something that is burning, but also for food and skin: Jeg brændte brødet (I burned the bread). Jeg brændte min hånd (I burned my hand).

sentence.da: Bålet kan **brænde** hele natten.
sentence.en: The campfire can burn all night.

at burde.explanation: "At burde" means "ought to", much like "should": Du bør hvile dig (You ought to rest). It says what is a good idea or a duty, not an order.

sentence.da: Du **burde** sove mere, fordi du er træt.
sentence.en: You should sleep more because you are tired.

at byde velkommen.explanation: "At byde velkommen" means "to welcome", for greeting guests or a group: Jeg byder jer velkommen (I welcome you). It sounds a bit formal, like in a speech.

sentence.da: Læreren vil **byde velkommen** til de nye elever.
sentence.en: The teacher wants to welcome the new students.

at bygge.explanation: "At bygge" means "to build", for a big thing like a house or a small thing like a birdhouse.

sentence.da: Man kan **bygge** et hus af træ.
sentence.en: You can build a house from wood.

at bygge om.explanation: "At bygge om" means "to rebuild" or "to convert", working on a building that already stands. Om adds the idea of doing something over in a new way, as in at lave om (to redo) and at flytte om (to rearrange).

sentence.da: Vi skal **bygge om** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: We are going to remodel the kitchen.

at bygge på.explanation: "At bygge på" means "to build on", or to add on: Vi bygger på huset (We are adding on to the house). It also means "to be based on": Filmen bygger på en bog (The film is based on a book).

forms.en: I have built on / added on

sentence.da: Vi vil **bygge på** huset, fordi vi får et barn.
sentence.en: We want to add on to the house because we are having a baby.

at bytte.explanation: "At bytte" means "to exchange" or "to swap", for example to get another size. It also works for swapping with someone: Vil du bytte plads? (Do you want to swap seats?)

sentence.da: Jeg vil **bytte** skjorten til en større.
sentence.en: I want to exchange the shirt for a bigger one.

at bære.explanation: "At bære" means "to carry", and also "to wear": Han bærer en tung kasse (He carries a heavy box). For clothes, Danes often say have på (to have on): Jeg har en jakke på (I am wearing a jacket).

sentence.da: Kan du **bære** min taske til bilen?
sentence.en: Can you carry my bag to the car?

at bøje.explanation: "At bøje" means "to bend", to make something curve or fold. To bend yourself down, add mig, dig or sig: Jeg bøjer mig (I bend down).

sentence.da: Du skal **bøje** knæene, når du løfter.
sentence.en: You have to bend your knees when you lift.

at børste tænder.explanation: "At børste tænder" means "to brush teeth". Danish says just tænder (teeth), with no word for my: Jeg børster tænder, while English says I brush my teeth.

sentence.da: Jeg skal **børste tænder** hver aften.
sentence.en: I have to brush my teeth every evening.

at bøvse.explanation: "At bøvse" means "to burp". The burp itself is en bøvs (a burp).

sentence.da: Babyen skal **bøvse** efter maden.
sentence.en: The baby has to burp after the meal.

bacon.explanation: "Bacon" means "bacon", salted pork cut in thin slices and fried. You count it in slices (skiver), not in pieces.

sentence.da: Jeg steger fire skiver **bacon** til morgenmad.
sentence.en: I fry four slices of bacon for breakfast.

badebukser.explanation: "Badebukser" means "swim trunks", the short pants that men and boys swim in. It is always plural, so one pair is et par badebukser (a pair of swim trunks).

sentence.da: Drenge har **badebukser** på, når de svømmer.
sentence.en: Boys wear swim trunks when they swim.

badetøj.explanation: "Badetøj" means "swimwear": swimsuits, swim trunks and other clothes you swim in. It is built from bade (to swim) and tøj (clothes). Like tøj, it is a group word for all the pieces together, so it has no plural.

sentence.da: Jeg tager **badetøj** og håndklæde med til stranden.
sentence.en: I am bringing swimwear and a towel to the beach.

badminton.explanation: "Badminton" means "badminton" and is the same word as in English.

sentence.da: Man spiller **badminton** med en ketsjer og en fjerbold.
sentence.en: You play badminton with a racket and a shuttlecock.

bag.explanation: "Bag" means "behind" and is always followed by a person or thing. On its own, use bagved (at the back): Katten sidder bagved (The cat is sitting at the back).

sentence.da: Barnet gemmer sig **bag** træet.
sentence.en: The child hides behind the tree.

bagage.explanation: "Bagage" means "luggage", all your bags and suitcases together. There is no plural, so bagager is not used. It is said ba-GAH-sheh. For one single bag, say en kuffert (a suitcase) or en taske (a bag).

sentence.da: Vi lander i lufthavnen og henter vores **bagage**.
sentence.en: We land at the airport and pick up our luggage.

bagefter.explanation: "Bagefter" means "afterwards". Compare efter maden (after the meal) with bagefter (afterwards): Vi spiser, og bagefter ser vi film (We eat, and afterwards we watch a film). Efter (after) needs a thing after it; bagefter stands alone.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser nu og vasker op **bagefter**.
sentence.en: I eat now and wash the dishes afterwards.

bagepapir.explanation: "Bagepapir" means "baking paper", the paper you put on a baking tray so the food does not stick.

sentence.da: Kagen sidder ikke fast, fordi jeg bruger **bagepapir**.
sentence.en: The cake does not stick, because I use baking paper.

bagepulver.explanation: "Bagepulver" means "baking powder", a white powder that makes a cake rise and turn out light.

sentence.da: Kagen hæver ikke uden **bagepulver**.
sentence.en: The cake does not rise without baking powder.

bagt.explanation: "Bagt" means "baked", cooked in the oven, the way bread and cake are. Food cooked in a pan is stegt (fried), not bagt.

sentence.da: Jeg laver **bagt** laks i ovnen.
sentence.en: I make baked salmon in the oven.

bagved.explanation: "Bagved" means "at the back". Compare Han står bag mig (He is standing behind me) with Han står bagved (He is standing at the back). With a thing after it, use bag.

forms.en: He is standing at the back.
The house is at the back.

sentence.da: Emma står **bagved** og ikke foran.
sentence.en: Emma stands at the back and not in front.

ballade.explanation: "Ballade" means "trouble" or "a fuss", usually loud trouble with people. A common phrase is at lave ballade (to make trouble).

sentence.da: Der er altid **ballade**, når børnene leger.
sentence.en: There is always a fuss when the children play.

balsam.explanation: "Balsam" means "conditioner" for hair, a cream you rub in after shampoo and rinse out again.

sentence.da: **Balsam** gør håret blødt og let at rede.
sentence.en: Conditioner makes hair soft and easy to comb.

bange.explanation: "Bange" means "afraid" or "scared". What you fear comes after for (of). Vær ikke bange means "Do not be afraid".

sentence.da: Jeg er meget **bange** i mørket.
sentence.en: I am very scared in the dark.

bange for.explanation: "Bange for" means "afraid of". It can also mean "I am afraid that...": Jeg er bange for, at det er sandt (I am afraid it is true).

forms.en: She is afraid of the dark.

forms.da: Er du bange for at flyve?

sentence.da: Børnene er **bange for** mørket.
sentence.en: The children are afraid of the dark.

barberskum.explanation: "Barberskum" means "shaving foam", the foam you put on your face before you shave. It is built from barbere (to shave) and skum (foam), and the same skum is in et skumbad (a bubble bath).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger **barberskum**, når jeg barberer mig.
sentence.en: I use shaving foam when I shave.

bare.explanation: "Bare" means "just" or "only". It often makes a sentence softer: Det er bare mig (It is just me). In an invitation it is friendly and means "go ahead": Kom bare ind (Come on in).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **bare** sove i dag.
sentence.en: I just want to sleep today.

basilikum.explanation: "Basilikum" means "basil", the herb used a lot in Italian food.

sentence.da: Vi plukker frisk **basilikum** til pizzaen.
sentence.en: We pick fresh basil for the pizza.

basketball.explanation: "Basketball" means "basketball", the team sport played with a big ball and a high hoop. The same word also names the ball: en basketball (a basketball).

sentence.da: Man kaster bolden i en kurv i **basketball**.
sentence.en: You throw the ball into a basket in basketball.

bedre.explanation: "Bedre" means "better". Use end (than) to compare: bedre end i går (better than yesterday). Jeg har det bedre means "I feel better".

sentence.da: Din nye cykel er **bedre** end den gamle.
sentence.en: Your new bike is better than the old one.

bedre sent end aldrig.explanation: "Bedre sent end aldrig" means "better late than never". Say it kindly when someone shows up late or finally does something: Tak, fordi du kom. Bedre sent end aldrig (Thanks for coming. Better late than never).

forms.da: Nå, men bedre sent end aldrig.
Han kom, og det er bedre sent end aldrig.
forms.en: He came, and better late than never.

sentence.da: Du kom for sent, men **bedre sent end aldrig**.
sentence.en: You came late, but better late than never.

bedst.explanation: "Bedst" means "best", the top one of all. It also says what you like most: Jeg kan bedst lide kaffe (I like coffee best).

sentence.da: Carl er **bedst** i klassen.
sentence.en: Carl is the best in the class.

bedst før.explanation: "Bedst før" means "best before". It is printed on food, which is often still fine for a while after that date. Fresh meat and fish say sidste anvendelsesdato (use-by date) instead.

forms.en: best before the end of June

sentence.da: Mælken er **bedst før** fredag.
sentence.en: The milk is best before Friday.

bedsteforældre.explanation: "Bedsteforældre" means "grandparents", the parents of your mother and father taken together. It is built from bedste (best) and forældre (parents), and one parent is en forælder (a parent).

sentence.da: Min mormor og min farfar er mine **bedsteforældre**.
sentence.en: My mother's mother and my father's father are my grandparents.

begge.explanation: "Begge" means "both" and is only for two. Compare Begge er her (Both are here) with Alle er her (Everyone is here, any number). Jeg kender dem begge to means "I know both of them".

sentence.da: Mine to børn er **begge** hjemme.
sentence.en: My two children are both at home.

behagelig.explanation: "Behagelig" means "comfortable" or "pleasant" and describes things that feel good. It also fits a voice or a temperature: en behagelig stemme (a pleasant voice), en behagelig temperatur (a pleasant temperature).

sentence.da: Sofaen er blød og **behagelig**.
sentence.en: The sofa is soft and comfortable.

beige.explanation: "Beige" means "beige", a light, sandy color like dry sand.

sentence.da: Sandet på stranden er **beige**.
sentence.en: The sand on the beach is beige.

bekendt.explanation: "Bekendt" means "familiar" or "known". The same word is also a person: en bekendt (an acquaintance) is someone you know a little, not a close friend.

sentence.da: Hendes stemme lyder **bekendt**.
sentence.en: Her voice sounds familiar.

benzin.explanation: "Benzin" means "gasoline", which Americans often call gas. A diesel car needs diesel instead.

sentence.da: Min bil kører på **benzin**, ikke på diesel.
sentence.en: My car runs on gasoline, not on diesel.

berømt.explanation: "Berømt" means "famous" and is stronger than kendt (well-known): Hun er berømt i hele verden (She is famous all over the world). Den er berømt for sin ost (It is famous for its cheese).

sentence.da: Hun er en **berømt** sanger i hele landet.
sentence.en: She is a famous singer all over the country.

beskadiget.explanation: "Beskadiget" means "damaged", used for things that have taken harm but can often still be used.

sentence.da: Bilen er **beskadiget** efter ulykken.
sentence.en: The car is damaged after the accident.

beskeden.explanation: "Beskeden" means "modest" and describes someone who does not brag: Hun er beskeden trods sin succes (She is modest despite her success). It can also mean small: en beskeden løn (a modest salary).

sentence.da: Hun er **beskeden** og snakker aldrig om sine succeser.
sentence.en: She is modest and never talks about her successes.

beskidt.explanation: "Beskidt" means "dirty". To say something got dirty, use blive (to become): Mine sko er blevet beskidte (My shoes have gotten dirty).

sentence.da: Man bliver **beskidt** af at lege i mudder.
sentence.en: You get dirty from playing in mud.

beskyttelse.explanation: "Beskyttelse" means "protection", something that keeps you safe from harm.

sentence.da: Solcreme giver **beskyttelse** mod solen.
sentence.en: Sunscreen gives protection from the sun.

bestemt.explanation: "Bestemt" means "for sure" and also "certain": Han kommer bestemt (He is coming for sure). A certain one is picked out: Jeg leder efter en bestemt bog (I am looking for a certain book).

forms.en: I definitely do not want to

sentence.da: Det er **bestemt** en god idé.
sentence.en: That is definitely a good idea.

bestik.explanation: "Bestik" means "cutlery": the knives, forks and spoons you eat with. It is used for the whole set, so for one piece you name it: en kniv (a knife), en gaffel (a fork) or en ske (a spoon).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger **bestik** og tallerkener på bordet.
sentence.en: I put cutlery and plates on the table.

bevidsthed.explanation: "Bevidsthed" means "consciousness", both being awake and being aware of something. Common phrases are at miste bevidstheden (to lose consciousness) and at komme til bevidsthed (to regain consciousness).

sentence.da: Efter ulykken kom han til **bevidsthed** igen.
sentence.en: After the accident he regained consciousness.

billig.explanation: "Billig" means "cheap". It can mean a low price or poor quality, and the situation usually makes clear which is meant. In a shop, you can ask Har du noget billigere? (Do you have something cheaper?).

sentence.da: Maden er **billig**, kun tyve kroner.
sentence.en: The food is cheap, only twenty kroner.

biologi.explanation: "Biologi" means "biology", the study of plants, animals and the human body. For a school class, you leave out en: Jeg er god til biologi (I am good at biology).

sentence.da: Vi lærer om dyr og planter i **biologi**.
sentence.en: We learn about animals and plants in biology.

bitter.explanation: "Bitter" means "bitter" for a taste like strong coffee: Kaffen er bitter (The coffee is bitter). It also fits a person who is still angry about something: Hun er bitter (She is bitter).

sentence.da: Kaffen er for **bitter** for mig.
sentence.en: The coffee is too bitter for me.

blandet.explanation: "Blandet" means "mixed", for things made of different kinds: en blandet salat (a mixed salad). It is also used for feelings: blandede følelser (mixed feelings).

sentence.da: Jeg køber **blandet** slik til børnene.
sentence.en: I buy mixed candy for the kids.

blandt.explanation: "Blandt" means "among" and is used with several people or things: Han er blandt de bedste (He is among the best). For just two things, use mellem (between): mellem huset og træet (between the house and the tree).

sentence.da: Katten gemmer sig **blandt** blomsterne.
sentence.en: The cat hides among the flowers.

blandt andet.explanation: "Blandt andet" means "among other things" and shows that your example is only one of several. It is often written bl.a.

forms.da: Vi talte blandt andet om musik.
forms.en: We talked about music, among other things.
among other things, that is why

sentence.da: Jeg købte **blandt andet** brød og ost.
sentence.en: I bought bread and cheese, among other things.

blank.explanation: "Blank" means "shiny": en blank overflade (a shiny surface). It also means "blank", like a page with nothing on it: et blankt ark (a blank sheet).

sentence.da: Bilen er **blank**, fordi jeg har vasket den.
sentence.en: The car is shiny because I washed it.

blind.explanation: "Blind" means "blind", for someone who cannot see: en blind mand (a blind man). Someone who cannot hear is døv (deaf).

sentence.da: Han er **blind** og kan ikke se.
sentence.en: He is blind and cannot see.

blod.explanation: "Blod" means "blood". The d is very soft, so it sounds close to blo. It is often part of longer words: blodprøve (blood test) and blodtryk (blood pressure).

sentence.da: Lægen tager en prøve af mit **blod**.
sentence.en: The doctor takes a sample of my blood.

blomkål.explanation: "Blomkål" means "cauliflower". It is built from blomst (flower) and kål (cabbage), so it literally means "flower cabbage". En blomkål is one whole head, and plain blomkål is the vegetable in general.

sentence.da: **Blomkål** er hvid og ligner en lille blomst.
sentence.en: Cauliflower is white and looks like a small flower.

blond.explanation: "Blond" means "blond", a light yellow hair color. It describes the hair itself or the person who has it.

sentence.da: Min søster er **blond**, men jeg har mørkt hår.
sentence.en: My sister is blond, but I have dark hair.

blot.explanation: "Blot" means "merely" or "just". It also appears in wishes: Havde jeg blot vidst det! (If only I had known!).

forms.en: He is only ten years old.

sentence.da: Jeg ville **blot** sige tak.
sentence.en: I just wanted to say thanks.

blå.explanation: "Blå" means "blue". Put lyse (light) or mørke (dark) in front to make shades: lyseblå means "light blue" and mørkeblå means "dark blue".

sentence.da: Himlen er **blå** i dag.
sentence.en: The sky is blue today.

blæsende.explanation: "Blæsende" means "windy", with strong wind blowing. It comes from at blæse (to blow), and "Det blæser" means "It is windy".

sentence.da: Det var en **blæsende** dag ved havet.
sentence.en: It was a windy day by the sea.

blæst.explanation: "Blæst" means "wind", the strong blowing you feel outdoors, as a kind of weather.

sentence.da: Der er meget **blæst** på stranden i dag.
sentence.en: There is a lot of wind on the beach today.

blød.explanation: "Blød" means "soft", pleasant to touch. It also describes a quiet, gentle sound: en blød stemme (a soft voice).

sentence.da: Jeg sover godt i en **blød** seng.
sentence.en: I sleep well in a soft bed.

borgerservice.explanation: "Borgerservice" means "Citizen Services": the municipal office for practical matters like a health insurance card, a passport or registering your address. It is written with a capital B, like the name of an office.

forms.en: I have to go to Citizen Services.

sentence.da: Jeg skal have nyt pas på **Borgerservice**.
sentence.en: I need a new passport at Citizen Services.

bortset fra.explanation: "Bortset fra" means "apart from" or "except". It names the one person or thing that does not fit what you just said.

sentence.da: Alle kom **bortset fra** Lars.
sentence.en: Everyone came except Lars.

bravo.explanation: "Bravo" means "bravo" and praises a performance or a good effort.

sentence.da: **Bravo**, det var en flot koncert!
sentence.en: Bravo, that was a great concert!

bred.explanation: "Bred" means "wide" or "broad", for how far something stretches from side to side: a road, a river, a smile.

sentence.da: Vejen er **bred**, ikke smal.
sentence.en: The road is wide, not narrow.

briller.explanation: "Briller" means glasses (for your eyes) and is only used in the plural. At have briller på means "to wear glasses".

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke læse uden mine **briller**.
sentence.en: I cannot read without my glasses.

britisk.explanation: "Britisk" means "British", from Great Britain. Do not mix it up with engelsk (English), which is about England and the English language.

sentence.da: Han bor i London og er **britisk**.
sentence.en: He lives in London and is British.

broccoli.explanation: "Broccoli" means "broccoli", a green vegetable with a thick stalk and many small tops.

sentence.da: **Broccoli** er grøn og ligner et lille træ.
sentence.en: Broccoli is green and looks like a little tree.

brugt.explanation: "Brugt" means "used" or "secondhand", for things that someone owned before you. It comes from at bruge (to use).

sentence.da: Jeg købte en **brugt** cykel på nettet.
sentence.en: I bought a used bike online.

brun.explanation: "Brun" means "brown". It is also used for a suntan: Du er blevet brun means "You have a tan".

sentence.da: Chokolade er **brun**, ikke hvid.
sentence.en: Chocolate is brown, not white.

brændstof.explanation: "Brændstof" means "fuel", for example for a car. It is built from brænde (to burn) and stof (material), and the same stof is in et sprængstof (an explosive).

sentence.da: Bilen bruger meget **brændstof** på motorvejen.
sentence.en: The car uses a lot of fuel on the highway.

brød.explanation: "Brød" means "bread". Et brød is one loaf, and plain brød is bread in general. With a number, it does not change: to brød (two loaves).

sentence.da: Jeg køber **brød** hos bageren.
sentence.en: I buy bread at the baker's.

bukser.explanation: "Bukser" means "pants" or "trousers". Like English "pants", it is always plural, so for one pair say et par bukser (a pair of pants).

sentence.da: Jeg har **bukser** og sko på.
sentence.en: I am wearing pants and shoes.

bulgur.explanation: "Bulgur" means "bulgur", cracked wheat that is boiled until soft.

sentence.da: Jeg laver en salat af **bulgur**, tomat og persille.
sentence.en: I make a salad of bulgur, tomato and parsley.

byttepenge.explanation: "Byttepenge" means "change", the money you get back when you pay more than the price. Like penge (money), it is always plural. It comes from at bytte (to exchange).

sentence.da: Du får 20 kroner i **byttepenge**.
sentence.en: You get 20 kroner in change.

både…og.explanation: "Både … og" means "both … and". Både goes before the first thing and og goes before the second. It joins two things of the same kind.

forms.da: både i dag og i morgen

sentence.da: Hun taler **både** dansk **og** engelsk.
sentence.en: She speaks both Danish and English.

bærbar.explanation: "Bærbar" means "portable", something you can carry. On its own, en bærbar means a laptop: Jeg har købt en ny bærbar (I bought a new laptop).

sentence.da: Min computer er **bærbar** og let at tage med.
sentence.en: My computer is portable and easy to take along.

bønner.explanation: "Bønner" means "beans". The same word also means prayers (from en bøn, a prayer), so the sentence shows which is meant.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser **bønner** og majs til aftensmad.
sentence.en: I eat beans and corn for dinner.

en baby.explanation: "En baby" means "a baby", someone only a few months or a year old.

sentence.da: Vores **baby** er to måneder gammel.
sentence.en: Our baby is two months old.

en babysitter.explanation: "En babysitter" means "a babysitter", someone who stays with kids for an evening.

sentence.da: En **babysitter** passer børnene, når vi er ude.
sentence.en: A babysitter looks after the children when we are out.

en backup.explanation: "En backup" means "a backup", a spare version of your files kept in case something breaks. To make one, say at tage en backup (to make a backup).

sentence.da: Jeg har lavet en **backup** af alle mine billeder.
sentence.en: I made a backup of all my pictures.

en badedragt.explanation: "En badedragt" means "a swimsuit", often the one-piece kind. For a two-piece, use en bikini (a bikini).

sentence.da: Jeg skal have min **badedragt** med til poolen.
sentence.en: I need to bring my swimsuit to the pool.

en bademåtte.explanation: "En bademåtte" means "a bath mat", the mat you step on when you get out of the shower. It is built from bade (to bathe) and måtte (mat), and bade also starts et badeværelse (a bathroom).

sentence.da: Husk at lægge en **bademåtte** foran badekarret.
sentence.en: Remember to put a bath mat in front of the bathtub.

en badestrand.explanation: "En badestrand" means "a bathing beach", a beach meant for swimming. It is built from at bade (to bathe) and strand (beach). A sign there may say Badning forbudt (No swimming).

sentence.da: Vi svømmer hver dag ved en lille **badestrand**.
sentence.en: We swim every day at a small bathing beach.

en badevægt.explanation: "En badevægt" means "a bathroom scale", used to check how heavy you are. It is built from bade (to bathe) and vægt (weight). Vægt on its own means weight: Hvad er din vægt? (What is your weight?)

sentence.da: Min **badevægt** viser, at jeg har tabt mig to kilo.
sentence.en: My bathroom scale shows that I have lost two kilos.

en bagagebærer.explanation: "En bagagebærer" means "a luggage rack" on a car roof, or "a bike rack" over the back wheel.

sentence.da: Min cykel har en **bagagebærer** til tasken.
sentence.en: My bike has a rack for the bag.

en bager.explanation: "En bager" means "a baker", the person who bakes bread and cakes. Danes say Jeg går til bageren (I am going to the baker's), literally to the baker, when they mean the shop.

sentence.da: En **bager** laver brød hver morgen.
sentence.en: A baker makes bread every morning.

en baggrund.explanation: "En baggrund" means "a background", the part behind something in a picture. It also means a person's past: Hun har en anden baggrund (She has a different background).

sentence.da: Billedet har en blå **baggrund**.
sentence.en: The picture has a blue background.

en baggård.explanation: "En baggård" means "a backyard" in a city: the shared space behind apartment buildings. It starts with bag (back).

sentence.da: Børnene leger i en **baggård** mellem husene.
sentence.en: The children play in a backyard between the houses.

en baglygte.explanation: "En baglygte" means "a taillight", the red light at the back of a car. It is also used for the red light on the back of a bicycle.

sentence.da: Din **baglygte** er rød, men forlygten er hvid.
sentence.en: Your taillight is red, but the headlight is white.

en baguette.explanation: "En baguette" means "a baguette", the long French bread with a crisp crust.

sentence.da: En **baguette** er et langt, tyndt brød fra Frankrig.
sentence.en: A baguette is a long, thin bread from France.

en bakke.explanation: "En bakke" means "a hill", a small rise in the land. It also means "a tray": Jeg bærer en bakke med kaffe (I carry a tray with coffee).

sentence.da: Det er hårdt at cykle op ad en **bakke**.
sentence.en: It is hard to bike up a hill.

en balance.explanation: "En balance" means "a balance", being steady or even. For the money in a bank account, use en saldo (a balance).

sentence.da: Det er vigtigt at finde en **balance** mellem arbejde og fritid.
sentence.en: It is important to find a balance between work and free time.

en balkon.explanation: "En balkon" means "a balcony", a small platform with a railing that sticks out from an upper floor of a building.

sentence.da: Vores lejlighed har en lille **balkon** mod gaden.
sentence.en: Our apartment has a small balcony facing the street.

en ballon.explanation: "En ballon" means "a balloon", a thin rubber bag. To blow one up, use at puste en ballon op (to blow up a balloon). Op (up) goes after the thing, like in at ringe nogen op (to call someone up).

sentence.da: En **ballon** er fuld af luft.
sentence.en: A balloon is full of air.

en bamse.explanation: "En bamse" means "a teddy bear". It can also be a friendly word for a big, cuddly person: Han er en rigtig bamse (He is a real teddy bear).

sentence.da: Min datter sover med sin **bamse**.
sentence.en: My daughter sleeps with her teddy bear.

en banan.explanation: "En banan" means "a banana". Say it with the stress on the last part: ba-NAN.

sentence.da: Aben spiser en gul **banan**.
sentence.en: The monkey eats a yellow banana.

en bane.explanation: "En bane" means "a court" or "a field" for sports. It also means "a track" where runners run or trains go: Løberne står klar på banen (The runners are ready on the track).

sentence.da: Vi spiller fodbold på en ny **bane** ved skolen.
sentence.en: We play soccer on a new field by the school.

en banegård.explanation: "En banegård" means "a railway station". It is built from bane (railway line) and gård (yard). With hoved (main) in front, en hovedbanegård (a main station) is the big central station of a city.

sentence.da: Vi venter på toget på en stor **banegård**.
sentence.en: We wait for the train at a big railway station.

en bank.explanation: "En bank" means "a bank", where you keep and handle money. Danes say at gå i banken (to go to the bank).

sentence.da: Jeg sætter mine penge ind i en **bank**.
sentence.en: I put my money into a bank.

en bankkonto.explanation: "En bankkonto" means "a bank account". It is built from bank (bank) and konto (account). Other accounts are named the same way, such as en opsparingskonto (a savings account) and en lønkonto (a salary account).

sentence.da: Jeg har penge på min **bankkonto**.
sentence.en: I have money in my bank account.

en barbermaskine.explanation: "En barbermaskine" means "an electric shaver". It is built from at barbere (to shave) and en maskine (a machine), the same maskine as in en vaskemaskine (a washing machine).

sentence.da: Han barberer sig hver morgen med en **barbermaskine**.
sentence.en: He shaves every morning with an electric shaver.

en barndom.explanation: "En barndom" means "a childhood", the years when you are small. To say when, use i (in): I min barndom boede vi på landet (In my childhood we lived in the country).

sentence.da: Jeg tænker ofte på min **barndom** hos mormor.
sentence.en: I often think of my childhood at Grandma's house.

en barndomsven.explanation: "En barndomsven" means "a childhood friend", a friend from when you were small. It is built from barndom (childhood) and ven (friend), and barndom also appears in et barndomshjem (a childhood home).

sentence.da: Han er min **barndomsven** fra børnehaven.
sentence.en: He is my childhood friend from kindergarten.

en barnepige.explanation: "En barnepige" means "a nanny" or "a babysitter". It is built from barn (child) and pige (girl), but a barnepige can also be a boy or a man: Min bror er barnepige i aften (My brother is the babysitter tonight).

sentence.da: Vores **barnepige** passer børnene i aften.
sentence.en: Our nanny is looking after the children tonight.

en barnevogn.explanation: "En barnevogn" means "a baby carriage", where a small baby lies down. For an older child who sits up, Danes use en klapvogn (a stroller).

sentence.da: Hun skubber en **barnevogn** ned ad gaden.
sentence.en: She pushes a baby carriage down the street.

en bedstefar.explanation: "En bedstefar" means "a grandfather" in general. In everyday speech, Danes usually say morfar (mother's father) or farfar (father's father), which tells you which side of the family he is on.

sentence.da: Min **bedstefar** er min mors far.
sentence.en: My grandfather is my mother's father.

en bedstemor.explanation: "En bedstemor" means "a grandmother" in general. In everyday speech, Danes usually say mormor (mother's mother) or farmor (father's mother). A short, warm form is bedste (grandma).

sentence.da: Min **bedstemor** er min fars mor.
sentence.en: My grandmother is my father's mother.

en begivenhed.explanation: "En begivenhed" means "an event", something special or important that takes place.

sentence.da: Festivalen er en stor **begivenhed** i byen.
sentence.en: The festival is a big event in the town.

en begravelse.explanation: "En begravelse" means "a funeral", the ceremony for a person who has died.

sentence.da: Der er en **begravelse** i kirken på lørdag.
sentence.en: There is a funeral in the church on Saturday.

en begyndelse.explanation: "En begyndelse" means "a beginning", the first part of something: i begyndelsen af filmen (at the beginning of the film). It is built from at begynde (to begin).

sentence.da: Et eventyr har en **begyndelse** og en slutning.
sentence.en: A fairy tale has a beginning and an ending.

en begynder.explanation: "En begynder" means "a beginner", someone who is new at something. It comes from at begynde (to begin).

sentence.da: Jeg er kun **begynder**, men jeg lærer hurtigt.
sentence.en: I am only a beginner, but I learn fast.

en behandling.explanation: "En behandling" means "a treatment". It comes from at behandle (to treat). It can also mean the way someone is treated, as in dårlig behandling (bad treatment).

sentence.da: Hun er syg og får **behandling** på sygehuset.
sentence.en: She is sick and is getting treatment at the hospital.

en bekendt.explanation: "En bekendt" means "an acquaintance", a person you have met a few times but are not close to: Han er en bekendt, ikke en nær ven (He is an acquaintance, not a close friend). It can also mean "familiar": Det er en bekendt sang (It is a familiar song).

sentence.da: Jeg mødte en **bekendt** i byen.
sentence.en: I met an acquaintance in town.

en bekymring.explanation: "En bekymring" means "a worry". In the same family are at bekymre sig (to worry) and Jeg er bekymret (I am worried).

sentence.da: Min største **bekymring** er pengene.
sentence.en: My biggest worry is the money.

en belønning.explanation: "En belønning" means "a reward", something you get for good work or a good deed.

sentence.da: Du får en **belønning**, når du er færdig.
sentence.en: You get a reward when you are done.

en benzinstation.explanation: "En benzinstation" means "a gas station", where you buy fuel for your car. It is built from benzin (gasoline) and station (station), the same station as in en politistation (a police station) and en brandstation (a fire station).

sentence.da: Bilen er næsten tom, og vi skal til en **benzinstation**.
sentence.en: The car is almost empty, and we have to go to a gas station.

en besked.explanation: "En besked" means "a message", or a piece of information someone passes on to you. Use at give besked (to let someone know) and at få besked (to be told).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **besked** til dig fra Anna.
sentence.en: I have a message for you from Anna.

en beslutning.explanation: "En beslutning" means "a decision", a choice you make after thinking. To make one, use at træffe (to make): Vi træffer en beslutning (We make a decision).

sentence.da: Det var en svær **beslutning** at flytte til udlandet.
sentence.en: It was a hard decision to move abroad.

en bestilling.explanation: "En bestilling" means "an order", something you ask a shop or restaurant to prepare or send. It comes from at bestille (to order).

sentence.da: Din **bestilling** er sendt, og den kommer i morgen.
sentence.en: Your order has been sent, and it is coming tomorrow.

en besøgende.explanation: "En besøgende" means "a visitor", someone who comes to a place for a short time.

sentence.da: Der er mange **besøgende** på museet i dag.
sentence.en: There are many visitors at the museum today.

en betaling.explanation: "En betaling" means "a payment", money given for something you buy or owe.

sentence.da: Vi har modtaget din **betaling**, tak.
sentence.en: We have received your payment, thanks.

en betjent.explanation: "En betjent" means "a police officer", a person who works for the police and keeps order.

sentence.da: En **betjent** arbejder for politiet og holder styr på trafikken.
sentence.en: A police officer works for the police and controls traffic.

en betydning.explanation: "En betydning" means "a meaning", what a word stands for. With stor (big) it means importance: Det har stor betydning (It matters a lot).

sentence.da: Jeg kender ikke ordets **betydning**.
sentence.en: I don't know the meaning of the word.

en bevægelse.explanation: "En bevægelse" means "a movement", either a motion of the body or a group working for a cause: en politisk bevægelse (a political movement).

sentence.da: Hun lavede en hurtig **bevægelse** med hånden.
sentence.en: She made a quick movement with her hand.

en bh.explanation: "En bh" means "a bra", a piece of underwear that supports the breasts.

sentence.da: En **bh** er en slags undertøj til kvinder.
sentence.en: A bra is a kind of underwear for women.

en bi.explanation: "En bi" means "a bee", a small flying insect. Bees are not wasps: en hveps (a wasp) is a different insect.

sentence.da: En **bi** summer rundt om blomsten.
sentence.en: A bee buzzes around the flower.

en bid.explanation: "En bid" means "a bite" of food. Add the food after it: en bid brød (a bite of bread).

sentence.da: Vil du have en **bid** af min kage?
sentence.en: Do you want a bite of my cake?

en bikini.explanation: "En bikini" means "a bikini", the two-piece swimsuit. For a one-piece, say en badedragt (a swimsuit).

sentence.da: På stranden har hun en rød **bikini** på.
sentence.en: On the beach she is wearing a red bikini.

en bil.explanation: "En bil" means "a car". At køre i bil means to go by car.

sentence.da: En **bil** har fire hjul og en motor.
sentence.en: A car has four wheels and an engine.

en bilist.explanation: "En bilist" means "a motorist", a person driving a car. It is bil (car) plus -ist, and -ist makes a word for a person in en turist (a tourist) and en pianist (a pianist).

sentence.da: En **bilist** skal altid holde tilbage for fodgængere.
sentence.en: A motorist must always yield to pedestrians.

en billet.explanation: "En billet" means "a ticket" for a train, bus, film or concert. You say at købe en billet (to buy a ticket).

sentence.da: Jeg har købt en **billet** til toget.
sentence.en: I have bought a ticket for the train.

en billetautomat.explanation: "En billetautomat" means "a ticket machine", the machine at a station where you buy a ticket yourself. It is built from billet (ticket) and automat (machine).

sentence.da: Du kan købe en billet ved en **billetautomat**.
sentence.en: You can buy a ticket at a ticket machine.

en billetkontrollør.explanation: "En billetkontrollør" means "a ticket inspector", a person who checks tickets on trains and buses. It is built from billet (ticket) and kontrollør (inspector).

sentence.da: En **billetkontrollør** tjekker billetterne i toget.
sentence.en: A ticket inspector checks the tickets on the train.

en bilnøgle.explanation: "En bilnøgle" means "a car key", the key that starts your car.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke køre, fordi jeg har mistet min **bilnøgle**.
sentence.en: I can't drive because I lost my car key.

en bilulykke.explanation: "En bilulykke" means "a car accident". It is built from bil (car) and ulykke (accident), and ulykke also appears in en arbejdsulykke (a work accident) and en flyulykke (a plane crash).

sentence.da: Der var en **bilulykke** på motorvejen i morges.
sentence.en: There was a car accident on the highway this morning.

en bilvask.explanation: "En bilvask" means "a car wash", a place with machines that clean your car.

sentence.da: Bilen er meget beskidt, og vi skal finde en **bilvask**.
sentence.en: The car is very dirty, and we have to find a car wash.

en biograf.explanation: "En biograf" means "a cinema", the place where you watch films. You say at gå i biografen (to go to the cinema). Danes often shorten it to bio, as in gå i bio (go to the cinema).

sentence.da: Vi ser en film i en stor **biograf**.
sentence.en: We watch a film in a big cinema.

en bjergbestigning.explanation: "En bjergbestigning" means "a mountain climb", the trip up a mountain on foot. It is built from bjerg (mountain) and bestigning (climbing up), and bjerg also appears in en bjergkæde (a mountain range).

sentence.da: Efter en lang **bjergbestigning** stod vi på toppen.
sentence.en: After a long mountain climb we stood on top.

en bjørn.explanation: "En bjørn" means "a bear": Bjørnen sover hele vinteren (The bear sleeps all winter). A polar bear is en isbjørn, built from is (ice) and bjørn.

sentence.da: En **bjørn** er stor og kan løbe hurtigt.
sentence.en: A bear is big and can run fast.

en blanding.explanation: "En blanding" means "a mixture", two or more things put together.

sentence.da: Dejen er en **blanding** af mel og vand.
sentence.en: The dough is a mixture of flour and water.

en blanket.explanation: "En blanket" means "a form" that you fill in, for example at the doctor's or the bank. To fill one in you say at udfylde en blanket (to fill in a form). Do not mix it up with en form, which means a shape.

sentence.da: Du skal udfylde denne **blanket**.
sentence.en: You have to fill in this form.

en ble.explanation: "En ble" means "a diaper", the soft pad a baby wears under its clothes. In British English it is a nappy. At skifte ble means to change a diaper.

sentence.da: Babyen har en våd **ble**.
sentence.en: The baby has a wet diaper.

en blender.explanation: "En blender" means "a blender", the machine for smoothies and soups.

sentence.da: Jeg laver en smoothie i min **blender**.
sentence.en: I make a smoothie in my blender.

en blodprøve.explanation: "En blodprøve" means "a blood test", a small sample of blood that is checked. It is built from blod (blood) and prøve (sample, test). You say at tage en blodprøve (to take a blood sample).

sentence.da: Lægen vil tage en **blodprøve**.
sentence.en: The doctor wants to take a blood sample.

en blog.explanation: "En blog" means "a blog", a website where someone writes posts. The writer is en blogger (a blogger).

sentence.da: Min søster skriver en **blog** om sin hund.
sentence.en: My sister writes a blog about her dog.

en blomme.explanation: "En blomme" means "a plum", a soft sweet fruit with a stone inside. Do not mix it up with en blomst (a flower): Jeg spiser en blomme, men jeg køber en blomst (I eat a plum, but I buy a flower).

sentence.da: Denne **blomme** er sød og lilla.
sentence.en: This plum is sweet and purple.

en blomst.explanation: "En blomst" means "a flower". It appears in compound words such as en blomsterbutik (a flower shop) and en blomstervase (a flower vase).

sentence.da: Hun plukker en smuk **blomst** i haven.
sentence.en: She picks a pretty flower in the garden.

en bluse.explanation: "En bluse" means "a blouse", a light top for a woman or girl. Do not mix it up with en skjorte (a shirt).

sentence.da: Hun har en rød **bluse** på.
sentence.en: She is wearing a red blouse.

en blyant.explanation: "En blyant" means "a pencil", a thin wooden writing tool with a gray core that you can erase. When the tip gets dull, you say at spidse en blyant (to sharpen a pencil).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver med en **blyant**.
sentence.en: I write with a pencil.

en bodylotion.explanation: "En bodylotion" means "a body lotion", a light cream for your whole body after a shower. To put it on, say Jeg smører mig ind (I rub lotion on myself).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger **bodylotion** efter badet, fordi min hud er tør.
sentence.en: I use body lotion after the bath because my skin is dry.

en bog.explanation: "En bog" means "a book", something you read, from a novel to a school book. The plural changes the vowel: to bøger (two books).

sentence.da: Man kan låne en **bog** på biblioteket.
sentence.en: You can borrow a book at the library.

en boghandel.explanation: "En boghandel" means "a bookstore", a shop that sells books. To borrow books for free, go to et bibliotek (a library) instead.

sentence.da: Jeg køber en roman i en **boghandel** i byen.
sentence.en: I buy a novel in a bookstore in town.

en bogreol.explanation: "En bogreol" means "a bookcase". It is built from bog (book) and reol (open rack), and reol also appears in en vinreol (a wine rack).

sentence.da: Vi har brug for en større **bogreol** til alle bøgerne.
sentence.en: We need a bigger bookcase for all the books.

en bold.explanation: "En bold" means "a ball", a round thing used in sports and games. To play with one, say at spille bold (to play ball).

sentence.da: Man kan sparke og kaste en **bold**.
sentence.en: You can kick and throw a ball.

en bolig.explanation: "En bolig" means "a home" in the sense of a place to live. For the feeling of home, use et hjem (a home): Vi har et rart hjem (We have a lovely home).

sentence.da: Vi leder efter en billig **bolig** i byen.
sentence.en: We are looking for a cheap home in the city.

en boligblok.explanation: "En boligblok" means "an apartment block", a building with many homes. It is built from bolig (home) and blok (block), and bolig also appears in et boligområde (a residential area).

sentence.da: Der bor mange familier i en **boligblok**.
sentence.en: Many families live in an apartment block.

en bolle.explanation: "En bolle" means "a bun" or "a bread roll". It can also mean a meatball in boller i karry (meatballs in curry), so the meaning depends on the dish.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **bolle** med smør.
sentence.en: I eat a bun with butter.

en bombe.explanation: "En bombe" means "a bomb". A bomb threat is en bombetrussel, built from bombe and en trussel (a threat).

sentence.da: Politiet fandt en **bombe** ved stationen.
sentence.en: The police found a bomb at the station.

en bon.explanation: "En bon" means "a receipt", especially the small paper one from the register. At the checkout you may hear Skal du have bonen med? (Do you want the receipt?).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler i kassen og får en **bon**.
sentence.en: I pay at the register and get a receipt.

en bonde.explanation: "En bonde" means "a farmer", someone who works the land and keeps animals.

sentence.da: En **bonde** står tidligt op og malker køerne.
sentence.en: A farmer gets up early and milks the cows.

en bordplade.explanation: "En bordplade" means "a tabletop" and also "a countertop" in a kitchen. It is built from bord (table) and plade (board).

sentence.da: Vi skal have en ny **bordplade** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: We need a new countertop in the kitchen.

en boremaskine.explanation: "En boremaskine" means "a drill". It is bore (to drill) plus maskine (machine). You use the verb like this: at bore et hul i væggen (to drill a hole in the wall).

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge en **boremaskine** til at lave et hul.
sentence.en: I need a drill to make a hole.

en borgmester.explanation: "En borgmester" means "a mayor", the person who leads a town or city. The leader of a whole country is en statsminister (a prime minister).

sentence.da: Byens **borgmester** holder en tale i dag.
sentence.en: The town's mayor gives a speech today.

en bowlinghal.explanation: "En bowlinghal" means "a bowling alley", a place with lanes where you roll a ball at pins.

sentence.da: Der er en **bowlinghal** i byen, hvor man kan spille bowling.
sentence.en: There is a bowling alley in town where you can play bowling.

en brand.explanation: "En brand" means "a fire" that is out of control: Der er brand i huset (There is a fire in the house). For a campfire, say et bål (a campfire).

sentence.da: Der var en stor **brand** i byen i nat.
sentence.en: There was a big fire in town last night.

en brandalarm.explanation: "En brandalarm" means "a fire alarm", the loud signal that warns of fire: Brandalarmen går (The fire alarm is going off). It is built from brand (fire) and alarm (alarm).

sentence.da: En **brandalarm** ringer højt, når der er røg.
sentence.en: A fire alarm rings loudly when there is smoke.

en brandbil.explanation: "En brandbil" means "a fire truck", the big red truck that goes to fires.

sentence.da: Der er ild i huset, og en **brandbil** kommer.
sentence.en: There is a fire in the house, and a fire truck is coming.

en brandmand.explanation: "En brandmand" means "a firefighter", a person who puts out fires.

sentence.da: En **brandmand** redder folk fra et brændende hus.
sentence.en: A firefighter rescues people from a burning house.

en brandslukker.explanation: "En brandslukker" means "a fire extinguisher". It is built from brand (fire) and at slukke (to put out), and at slukke also means to switch off: at slukke lyset (to turn off the light).

sentence.da: Brug en **brandslukker**, hvis det brænder.
sentence.en: Use a fire extinguisher if something is burning.

en brandstation.explanation: "En brandstation" means "a fire station", the building where firefighters and their trucks wait for emergency calls. It is built from brand (fire) and station (station).

sentence.da: Brandbilen holder foran den lille **brandstation**.
sentence.en: The fire truck is parked in front of the small fire station.

en bredde.explanation: "En bredde" means "a width", how far something measures from side to side. Length and width are often said together: længde og bredde (length and width).

sentence.da: Vinduet har en **bredde** på to meter.
sentence.en: The window has a width of two meters.

en bremse.explanation: "En bremse" means "a brake", the part that slows a car or a bike. The same word is also the action: at bremse (to brake).

sentence.da: En **bremse** får bilen til at stoppe.
sentence.en: A brake makes the car stop.

en brevsprække.explanation: "En brevsprække" means "a mail slot", the narrow opening in a door with a flap, where the mail is pushed through. It is built from brev (letter) and sprække (slit).

sentence.da: Posten falder på gulvet gennem en **brevsprække**.
sentence.en: The mail falls onto the floor through a mail slot.

en bro.explanation: "En bro" means "a bridge", something you cross over a river, road or sea.

sentence.da: Vi går over en **bro** over vandet.
sentence.en: We walk over a bridge over the water.

en brochure.explanation: "En brochure" means "a brochure", a small printed booklet with information, for example from a hotel or a travel company.

sentence.da: Hotellet sendte mig en **brochure** med mange billeder.
sentence.en: The hotel sent me a brochure with many pictures.

en bror.explanation: "En bror" means "a brother". Danish has separate words for older and younger: storebror (big brother) and lillebror (little brother), as in Min lillebror er fem år (My little brother is five years old).

sentence.da: Min **bror** og jeg har samme mor.
sentence.en: My brother and I have the same mother.

en brownie.explanation: "En brownie" means "a brownie", a small, dense chocolate cake that is cut into squares. It is often served warm.

sentence.da: En **brownie** er en kage med meget chokolade.
sentence.en: A brownie is a cake with a lot of chocolate.

en browser.explanation: "En browser" means "a browser", the program you use to open web pages.

sentence.da: Jeg åbner min **browser** og søger efter opskriften.
sentence.en: I open my browser and search for the recipe.

en brudepige.explanation: "En brudepige" means "a bridesmaid", a girl or woman who helps the bride on the wedding day.

related.en: a best man / maid of honor

sentence.da: Min søster skal være **brudepige** til brylluppet.
sentence.en: My sister is going to be a bridesmaid at the wedding.

en brudgom.explanation: "En brudgom" means "a groom", the man who is getting married. The couple together are et brudepar (a bridal couple).

related.en: a best man / maid of honor

sentence.da: Han er en glad **brudgom** på sin bryllupsdag.
sentence.en: He is a happy groom on his wedding day.

en bruger.explanation: "En bruger" means "a user", a person who uses an app, a website or a service. It is built from at bruge (to use), which also means to spend: at bruge penge (to spend money).

sentence.da: Hver **bruger** har sin egen adgangskode.
sentence.en: Every user has their own password.

en brugsanvisning.explanation: "En brugsanvisning" means "a user manual", the paper that explains how to use a product.

sentence.da: Jeg læser en **brugsanvisning**, fordi maskinen er ny.
sentence.en: I am reading a user manual because the machine is new.

en brunch.explanation: "En brunch" means "a brunch", a big breakfast eaten late in the morning. A normal early breakfast is morgenmad (breakfast).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **brunch** sent om søndagen.
sentence.en: We eat brunch late on Sundays.

en bruser.explanation: "En bruser" means "a shower", the fixture you stand under. With a badekar (bathtub) you lie down instead.

sentence.da: Der er en ny **bruser** på badeværelset.
sentence.en: There is a new shower in the bathroom.

en bryllupsdag.explanation: "En bryllupsdag" means "a wedding anniversary", the day each year when a couple married. It is built from bryllup (wedding) and dag (day), and bryllup also appears in en bryllupsgave (a wedding gift) and en bryllupsfest (a wedding party).

sentence.da: I dag er det vores **bryllupsdag**, og vi spiser ude.
sentence.en: Today is our wedding anniversary, and we are eating out.

en bryllupsrejse.explanation: "En bryllupsrejse" means "a honeymoon", the journey a couple takes after the wedding. It is built from bryllup (wedding) and rejse (journey), and rejse is also a verb: at rejse (to travel).

sentence.da: Vi vil på **bryllupsrejse** til Italien i maj.
sentence.en: We want to go on our honeymoon to Italy in May.

en brødkniv.explanation: "En brødkniv" means "a bread knife", the long knife with small teeth that cuts bread without crushing it.

sentence.da: Han skærer det friske brød med en **brødkniv**.
sentence.en: He cuts the fresh bread with a bread knife.

en brødkurv.explanation: "En brødkurv" means "a bread basket", a basket for bread or rolls that stands on the table at a meal. It is built from brød (bread) and kurv (basket).

sentence.da: Vi lægger brødet i en **brødkurv**.
sentence.en: We put the bread in a bread basket.

en brødrister.explanation: "En brødrister" means "a toaster". It is built from brød (bread) and at riste (to toast), and at riste is also in ristede løg (crispy fried onions).

sentence.da: En **brødrister** gør brødet varmt og sprødt.
sentence.en: A toaster makes the bread warm and crispy.

en brøk.explanation: "En brøk" means "a fraction", a part of a whole in math.

sentence.da: En fjerdedel af en pizza er en **brøk**.
sentence.en: A quarter of a pizza is a fraction.

en buffet.explanation: "En buffet" means "a buffet", a long table with many dishes where you serve yourself. A hotel often has one for breakfast, usually for one fixed price.

sentence.da: Vi tager selv mad fra den store **buffet**.
sentence.en: We take food ourselves from the big buffet.

en bund.explanation: "En bund" means "a bottom", the lowest part of something, such as a pan, a box or the sea. It is also the base of a pie: en tærtebund (a pie crust).

sentence.da: En kop har en flad **bund**.
sentence.en: A cup has a flat bottom.

en bunke.explanation: "En bunke" means "a pile", things lying on top of each other in no neat order: en bunke tøj (a pile of clothes). It also means "a large amount": en bunke penge (a large amount of money).

sentence.da: En **bunke** er rodet, men en stak er pæn.
sentence.en: A pile is messy, but a stack is neat.

en burger.explanation: "En burger" means "a burger", a patty of meat in a bun, usually with salad and sauce. A vegetarian one is en vegetarburger (a vegetarian burger).

sentence.da: En **burger** er kød mellem to stykker brød.
sentence.en: A burger is meat between two pieces of bread.

en bus.explanation: "En bus" means "a bus". To say you go by bus, use at tage bussen (to take the bus) or at køre med bus (to travel by bus).

sentence.da: En **bus** har plads til mange mennesker.
sentence.en: A bus has room for many people.

en busbillet.explanation: "En busbillet" means "a bus ticket", the ticket for riding the bus. It is built from bus (bus) and billet (ticket), and billet also appears in en biografbillet (a cinema ticket) and en koncertbillet (a concert ticket).

sentence.da: Du skal bruge en **busbillet** i bussen.
sentence.en: You need a bus ticket on the bus.

en buschauffør.explanation: "En buschauffør" means "a bus driver". The word chauffør (driver) works for other vehicles too: en taxachauffør (a taxi driver), en lastbilchauffør (a truck driver).

sentence.da: En **buschauffør** kører bussen hele dagen.
sentence.en: A bus driver drives the bus all day.

en busk.explanation: "En busk" means "a bush", a low plant with many stems growing close to the ground.

sentence.da: Bærrene vokser på en **busk**.
sentence.en: The berries grow on a bush.

en butik.explanation: "En butik" means "a shop", usually a smaller one that sells one kind of thing, such as clothes or shoes. For a big shop with food and everyday things, Danes say et supermarked (a supermarket).

sentence.da: Jeg køber sko i en **butik** i byen.
sentence.en: I buy shoes in a shop in town.

en butiksindehaver.explanation: "En butiksindehaver" means "a shop owner", the person who owns and runs a shop. It is built from butik (shop) and indehaver (holder), and indehaver is used for any holder: indehaveren af kortet (the holder of the card).

sentence.da: Han er **butiksindehaver** og åbner selv butikken hver morgen.
sentence.en: He is a shop owner and opens the shop himself every morning.

en by.explanation: "En by" means "a town" or "a city". Danish uses one word for both, so it can be small or big. I byen means "in town", and Jeg skal ind til byen means "I am going into town".

sentence.da: Der er mange huse i en **by**.
sentence.en: There are many houses in a town.

en bydel.explanation: "En bydel" means "a district", one part of a city. It is built from by (town) and del (part), and del also builds en landsdel (a region of a country) and en verdensdel (a continent).

sentence.da: Vi bor i en rolig **bydel** nær havnen.
sentence.en: We live in a quiet part of town near the harbor.

en byge.explanation: "En byge" means "a shower", a sudden, short spell of wet weather. For washing yourself, use et brusebad (a shower).

sentence.da: Der kom en kraftig **byge**, og vi blev våde.
sentence.en: A heavy shower came and we got wet.

en byggeplads.explanation: "En byggeplads" means "a construction site". It is built from bygge (build) and plads (place), and plads also appears in en parkeringsplads (a parking lot) and en legeplads (a playground).

sentence.da: De bygger et nyt hus på en **byggeplads**.
sentence.en: They are building a new house on a construction site.

en båd.explanation: "En båd" means "a boat", from a small rowboat to a bigger one. For a big ship, Danish uses et skib (a ship).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **båd** til øen.
sentence.en: We are taking a boat to the island.

en bæltetaske.explanation: "En bæltetaske" means "a fanny pack", a small zipped pouch that you wear around your waist, handy when you travel.

sentence.da: Hun bærer en lille **bæltetaske** om livet.
sentence.en: She carries a small fanny pack around her waist.
